To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SQL extensions are a powerful and flexible approach for adding new functionality to DBMSs.

1) a simple extension of the SQL query language to support new table functions and aggregate functions is sufficient for a wide range of database applications, including data mining and stream-oriented processing; 2) the new aggregate functions and table functions can be expressed in SQL and can be implemented in a database system using the same techniques as the built-in SQL aggregate functions and table operations; and 3) the SQL extension is conducive to both performance and data independence, and can be supported in a DBMS
we have designed a native extension of SQL that can be used to express a variety of data mining tasks, and we have developed a system to realize this extension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a native, declarative extension to SQL for data mining and other new applications, which are conducive to performance, extensibility, and data independence.
the design and implementation of a new native data mining language, ATLaS, which is an extension of SQL.
the development of a general mechanism for extending SQL, which is conducive to performance and is conducive to data independence.

this paper provides a comprehensive and detailed analysis of the need for a native SQL data mining extension, and the architecture for a native SQL extension.
the proposed extensions to SQL can provide the necessary expressive power and extensiveness to support new applications, particularly data mining, in a DBMS.

the proposed extensions of the SQL-3 language, which are based on a native extension model (ATLaS), provide a general and flexible framework for extending SQL to support a wide range of new application areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SQL extensions we have developed are very powerful and flexible, and can be implemented efficiently.
we have developed a native extension of SQL for data mining, which is called ATLaS (Aggregation, Time Series and Stream Processing in SQL).
ATLaS is the first SQL-based native extension of SQL for data mining.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SQL can be extended in a simple, yet powerful, way, to deal with new application areas and to support data mining.
it is possible to provide a powerful native extension mechanism for database query languages, and to implement it efficiently in commercial DBMSs.
the SQL language can be easily extended to support new application areas, and that these extensions do not have to compromise the data independence and performance of the DBMS.
